mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi replacement engine typically costs £650-£1,300 for a used unit, £1,200-£1,900 for a reconditioned unit, or £1,800-£3,200 for a rebuilt unit with 12-month warranty. Supply & fit labour adds approximately £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of AdBlue system failure in a Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is the "Urea fault" or "AdBlue fault" warning message, followed by the car entering reduced-power limp mode despite the AdBlue tank being full. Other symptoms include engine management lights and, eventually, prevention of engine starting.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 508 2.0 BlueHDi worth £6,000-£16,000, replacement is often worthwhile if the rest of the car is in good condition. If the vehicle is worth under £6,000, a used engine or targeted repair may be more cost-effective. The 2.0 BlueHDi is considered the most reliable and well-balanced engine of this generation.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi engines are dispatched within 24-48 hours, with supply & fit installation typically completed within 1-2 working days at approved garages.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi replacement engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rebuilt Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi engines include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically carry 3-6 months cover depending on supplier terms. Always verify warranty terms before purchase.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 2.0 BlueHDi and the 1.5 BlueHDi in the Peugeot 508?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) was fitted to both first- and second-generation 508s (2011-2024) and produces 150-180hp, offering strong torque for towing and motorway driving. The 1.5 BlueHDi (DV5) replaced the 1.6 BlueHDi on the second-generation 508 (2018 onwards), offering 130hp with improved emissions but introducing its own AdBlue-related failure points.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 2.0 BlueHDi joined the Peugeot 508 range as the torque-rich diesel option, offered in 150hp and 180hp outputs across both first- and second-generation models. It replaced the earlier 2.0 HDi with improved emissions technology and became the preferred choice for towing and high-mileage UK driving.

milestones.description: 2.0 BlueHDi (150hp) launched with the Gen 1 508 saloon and SW estate
2.0 BlueHDi (180hp) introduced with DW10FC engine code (AHW) for higher-output variants
Facelift styling with BlueHDi emissions technology for Euro 6 compliance
2.0 BlueHDi continued into Gen 2 508 with updated DW10FC variants (AHX, EHZ)
2.0 BlueHDi production ends with the Gen 2 508

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi is a robust and well-balanced diesel engine, but AdBlue system failures, water pump issues and DPF regeneration problems dominate replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Use the problem groups below to compare repair costs versus replacement value for your specific 2.0 BlueHDi.

problems.h4: AdBlue System Failure - Why DW10FC 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Enter Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue injector crystallises or the tank/pump assembly fails, triggering SCR system faults and forcing the engine into reduced-power limp mode to meet emissions compliance.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injector, clean crystallisation or replace unit; reset SCR adaptation
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before pump damage; may recur on short journeys

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace complete tank/pump module; refill AdBlue; perform SCR calibration
repairOptions.longevity: Addresses root cause; recommended if injector fault recurs or pump shows wear

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt DW10FC with Updated SCR Components
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with upgraded AdBlue injector and SCR calibration, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine has other wear items or 100k+ miles; eliminates repeat SCR issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi of 2014-2022 vintage is worth approximately £6,000-£16,000 depending on mileage and condition【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. For vehicles worth £6,000-£10,000, a used engine or targeted AdBlue repair typically offers better value than a full rebuilt unit. For vehicles worth over £10,000, a rebuilt engine with updated SCR components justifies the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: On a Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi, replacing the AdBlue tank/pump assembly is cost-effective if the engine is otherwise healthy. If the vehicle has exceeded 100,000 miles or shows additional diesel wear signs, a rebuilt DW10FC with updated SCR components offers better long-term reliability.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DW10FC Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: Water Pump Failure - Why 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Overheat
problems.rootCause: The water pump on 2.0 BlueHDi units is known to fail, with the temperature warning light illuminating as the first sign. Plastic impellers can degrade, reducing coolant flow and causing overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove old pump; fit new OEM-spec unit; flush cooling system; refill coolant
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Water Pump + Timing Belt Service
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump and timing belt together; full cooling system service
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended preventative maintenance at 100k miles; saves labour versus separate jobs

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt DW10FC with New Cooling System
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with new water pump and cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine has 100k+ miles or shows additional wear

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi worth £6,000-£16,000, water pump replacement is cost-effective if the engine is otherwise sound. Replacing the timing belt at the same time is a sensible preventative measure.
problems.recommendation: If your 2.0 BlueHDi shows the temperature warning light or coolant loss, have the water pump inspected immediately. If the vehicle has exceeded 100,000 miles, replacing the water pump and timing belt together offers the best value and prevents future failures.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DW10FC Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: DPF Regeneration Failure - Why 2.0 BlueHDi Diesels Lose Power
problems.rootCause: Short-journey driving prevents active DPF regeneration, causing soot accumulation that blocks exhaust flow and triggers power-limiting fault codes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic-led forced DPF burn; clean EGR valve; reset adaptation
repairOptions.longevity: Works if blockage is mild and driving patterns change

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove DPF; thermal/chemical clean; pressure test; reinstall with new gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Extends DPF life 30k-50k miles if driving habits improve

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt DW10FC with DPF Service
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt DW10FC unit; include DPF clean or replacement; 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine shows additional wear or DPF is beyond cleaning

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Peugeot 508 2.0 BlueHDi used primarily for motorway driving, a professional DPF clean often resolves the issue cost-effectively. For urban-use vehicles with recurring DPF warnings, a rebuilt diesel engine with updated DPF and EGR components provides more reliable long-term ownership.
problems.recommendation: If your 2.0 BlueHDi is used mainly for short urban trips, consider a forced regeneration and EGR clean first. If DPF warnings recur within 12 months or the vehicle is high-mileage, a rebuilt DW10FC with upgraded components eliminates the repeat risk.
